<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getMetaTypes (symbol, a method of class ProtocolDiscoveryAndBasesFacet))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via getMetaTypes (symbol, a method of class ProtocolDiscoveryAndBasesFacet))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via metadataForms (literal, a string literal in walkMetadataForms))_
- `content/docs/ui/reports.mdx`  _(via LABEL (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`  _(via metadataForms (literal, a string literal in walkMetadataForms))_

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class), metadataForms (literal, a string literal in walkMetadataForms))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 97e0f934e5e0613179a429ce9fcaa47e2d351768` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9564f2ffa652853cd99bf35c017614c887bfc09f` — the merge of head `597f70e74069d518950e6ea574de3ac32c71e2e1` into base `97e0f934e5e0613179a429ce9fcaa47e2d351768`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9564f2ffa652853cd99bf35c017614c887bfc09f && git checkout 9564f2ffa652853cd99bf35c017614c887bfc09f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 97e0f934e5e0613179a429ce9fcaa47e2d351768 597f70e74069d518950e6ea574de3ac32c71e2e1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 97e0f934e5e0613179a429ce9fcaa47e2d351768 && git merge --no-ff 597f70e74069d518950e6ea574de3ac32c71e2e1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 97e0f934e5e0613179a429ce9fcaa47e2d351768
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 97e0f934e5e0613179a429ce9fcaa47e2d351768` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `597f70e74069d518950e6ea574de3ac32c71e2e1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, packages/spec/src/system/index.ts, packages/spec/src/system/metadata-list-registry.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/system/metadata-list-zod-reconciliation.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-discovery-and-bases.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-type-schema.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-types-listing.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-list-layout-36860.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-types-list-headers.test.ts, packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts, scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/servedListColumns.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceListPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/registry.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/useMetadata.ts, the two app-shell tests, the generated spec shards (api-surface, authorable-surface, declaration-map, export-origins, json-schema.manifest) and content/docs/references, .changeset/36860-metadata-list-columns.md
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Inputs: card #36860 body and all six comments (7122720706, 7122828117, 7122844515, 7122871023, 7123560039, 7124466797), the PR body, the 32-file net diff against merge-base `5c2e34cdb2b4`, and the head's check-runs. The tree touches `packages/spec/src/**`, so the face is the published schema and the record carries ④; the brief named the declaration shape, the committed tree decides the tier.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`MetadataListCellTypeSchema`, `MetadataListColumnSchema`, `MetadataListViewSchema`, `defineList` and their six types (`@objectstack/spec/ui`): right.** New names only. The column is `ListColumnSchema.pick(field, label, type)` with `type` re-declared as a closed six-value enum; `ListColumnSchema.type` is a free string on `main`, so every value a metadata column accepts is one a `ListColumn` already accepts. The view is `ListViewShapeSchema.pick(data, columns)` with `columns` narrowed to at least one metadata column. Both stay strict, so `width` and the other ListView keys are refused (pinned by the "gate can fail" case). No accept-set on any existing schema moves.
- **`METADATA_LIST_REGISTRY`, `MetadataListType`, `resolveMetadataListLabels` (`@objectstack/spec/system`): right.** A frozen const beside `METADATA_FORM_REGISTRY`, one entry (`hook`: name, label, object, events, priority, async, description). All seven keys are declared on `HookSchema` at head (`hook.zod.ts` 555 to 684) and all seven are fields of `hook.form.ts` with no explicit label, so each header equals the humanized form label and no bundle leaf is new. The resolver returns a new object, rewrites `label` only, and leaves a list untouched when the bundle has no entry for the type.
- **`GetMetaTypesResponseSchema.entries[].list` optional: right.** Additive on a non-strict entry object; a client that ignores it parses as before. The dev's note that `schema` and `form` are still undeclared there is accurate and stays out of scope.
- **`getMetaTypes()` serves `list` beside `form`, omitted when the type has none: right.** Both emit sites carry it, the `MetaTypesListingEntry` pin gains `list?`, and the protocol test holds the control (no `list` key on an undeclared type).
- **`translateMetaTypesResponse` translates the headers through `metadataForms.TYPE.fields.FIELD.label`: right.** Same bundle, locale and options as `form`; the rest test pins zh-CN, a dotted path, the en control, a type with no list and no in-place mutation.
- **`walkMetadataForms` step 3 and the `METADATA_LIST_REGISTRY_MODULE` coupling constant: right by reading.** The de-duplication key matches the entry shape `walkFormField` pushes (`['metadataForms', type, 'fields', path, 'label']`, source `metadataFormField`), so a column the form labels emits nothing and a column it does not emits one leaf with the header as source. The constant follows the two bare constants already there. See N2: on this head the branch has no input.
- **Generated shards and reference docs: right.** They list exactly the new names and the five keys `ui/MetadataListColumn:field|label|type`, `ui/MetadataListView:columns|data`; `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · docs & code guards` and `Build Docs` are green on the head.
- **`engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: right.** Three ledger rows for the new metadata-protocol test file, nothing else.
- **Console precedence (`servedListColumns`): right.** Served list, else the console `listColumns`, else the default; `listExtraColumns` appended after any of the three with key de-duplication. For `hook` no console declaration exists on `main`, so the only visible change is the Hooks list. A type that serves no list reads exactly the expression it read before.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, each `minor`. These are every package whose source the diff touches; `scripts/**` and `content/docs/**` publish nothing. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: new exports and one new optional served key; nothing accepted before is refused. It is present in the PR body and the changeset body.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` is right, and nothing here is `semantic`. No existing key changes meaning or default. The authorable ratchet gains five keys, which is `added` by AGENTS.md step 3, and `added` takes at least `minor`, which every listed package has. No author-facing door accepts a `MetadataListView` yet (only the spec's own registry calls `defineList`), so `none` was arguable; `added` is the conservative reading and costs nothing.
- `Skills-docs: none` with its reason is on both the changeset and the PR body (the body line was added after the dev report, without a head move). Its truth is judged in ③.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`: empty.** Nothing to answer.
- **Seat route 7122844515, four points: followed.** (1) Shape: `ListViewShapeSchema` and `ListColumnSchema` narrowed through `defineList`, no new shape. (2) Label source: the existing `fields.KEY.label` slot; no new translation slot, and the extractor emits that slot for a column the form does not label. (3) Absent keys: `schemaDefaultAt` reads the served JSON Schema default at the column path, pinned for `priority` and `async`. (4) `flow`: not declared in (a); the report states `type` only for (b).
- **`Skills-docs: none`: true on this head, and no skills follow-up is owed by (a).** Read at head: outside `packages/spec` nothing calls `defineList` or imports `MetadataListViewSchema` / `MetadataListColumnSchema`. The only caller is `metadata-list-registry.ts`; the only other reference is the response schema's `list`. There is no loader, no registrar, no metadata type and no stack-definition key through which an app or plugin author's list declaration is consumed, and the registry is a frozen module constant. An author can import `defineList` and build a value, but nothing loads it. `skills/**` at head teaches no Studio metadata list columns (its only hits are the record-page `relatedListColumns`, a different surface). The five `authorable-surface/ui.json` rows are the ratchet's mechanical ledger of the keys of every exported strict object schema in the category; it does not test for a door, and listing them is correct and required by the gate. The export therefore does not make `none` untrue. Two things follow. The body's own words "a metadata author cannot write it" sit beside `Metadata-protocol: added`, whose definition is what an author can write: the `added` rests on the ratchet count alone and is the conservative choice (② above); it is not evidence of a door. And the skills debt starts the day a door opens: the card that adds a list registrar or a stack key owes `Skills-docs` then, not this one (N4).
- **Plugin registrar: correctly absent.** No registrar is added; the registry is frozen; the PR body says so.
- **`Part of #36860`: right for split (a).** The card's acceptance for Flows, Jobs, the 9 console types, `object`, and the zh screenshots is not met by this PR and is named for (b), which carries `Fixes`. The split and its line counts are on the card (7123560039).
- **Corrected and dropped columns (report 7124466797): nothing in (a) is made false by them.** The registry holds `hook` only, and the reconciliation test asserts exactly `['hook']`, so (b) must edit that assertion to add a type. One comment is made false meanwhile (N3).
- **Dev flag, out-of-scope 1 (`schema` and `form` undeclared on the response schema):** accurate, pre-existing, not widened here. The seat files it.
- **Dev flag, out-of-scope 2 (the runtime dispatcher serves `form`, and now `list`, untranslated):** accurate and pre-existing for `form`, but it has one new consequence in (a), recorded as N1. The seat files it with that consequence named.
- **Security: no new exposure.** `list` is a compile-time constant of column keys and English labels, a subset of what the same entry already serves as `schema` and `form`. The diff changes no route registration and no guard: the REST route and the dispatcher's `/meta` domain keep their existing caller gates. Header translation reads the bundle the same call already reads for `form`. Cells read the row body the list read already returns whole.
- **SQL push-down: not applicable.** The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; the served value is a module constant and the console reads rows it already fetched.
- **Author:** the PR `user.login` was not read as an input; the body is signed by the dev session `session_01WGufzg7mFFG5b13DcQ93kf` through the relay.

### ④ Design judgment

Each `hits` file holds against the seat route and its first consumer (Studio's generic list, proven on `hook`). Nits and accepted deviations, none affecting correctness or the contract on this head:

- **N1 (accepted deviation, goes on the dispatcher card).** `servedListColumns` marks every served header `labelLocalized: true` whether or not the server translated it. Where the listing is served untranslated (the runtime dispatcher path, or a host with no translation bundle), a zh reader of the Hooks list now sees `Name / Label / Description` where the console's own `engine.list.col.*` table gave `名称 / 显示名 / 描述` before. On the REST path with the shipped bundles the headers are translated. Part (b) widens this to 27 types, so the dispatcher card should land before or with (b), or (b) should fall back to the console table when a served header equals its English source.
- **N2 (carry to (b)).** The extractor's list-column branch in `i18n-walk.ts` emits nothing on this head (every `hook` column is a form field) and no lint test pins it. It reads correct. Part (b) gives it its first input and owes the pin: one column path the form does not declare emits one leaf, and a path the form declares emits none.
- **N3 (prose).** `registry.ts` now says the columns reading `listInclude: 'grants'` are the type's own `listExtraColumns`; `position` still declares `_holderCount` and `_grantedPermissionSets` under `listColumns` in the untouched `builtinComponents.tsx`. True only after (b).
- **N4 (carry to the registrar card).** `defineList` is exported and its jsdoc does not say that only the spec's own registry is read. No skill should teach it until a door consumes an author's declaration; the card that opens one owes the skills and docs update and should say so in its `Skills-docs:` line.
- **N5.** `MetadataListViewSchema` inherits `data` as picked: optional, any provider arm. Only `defineList` forces `provider: 'schema'`, and no consumer in the diff reads `data`. Accepted under the seat's shape-reuse ruling (one declaration can feed the record grid later); if a second producer appears, narrow `data` to the schema arm.
- **N6.** `MetadataListType` is `keyof` a `Record` keyed by `string`, so it is `string`, not a union. Same as `MetadataFormType`; parity, not a defect.
- **N7.** The reconciliation test hand-copies `humanizeFieldPath` from `@objectstack/lint`. A drift between the two would show as a header mismatch only for a column the form does not label, which (b) introduces.

Check-runs on the head: 71 names, latest run each; all `success` except nine `skipped` (opt-in, queue-only and matrix-parent lanes). None failed, none pending.
